messages:
emma: Quick sync — we need final API shape and launch guards for the Rerank endpoint today. Customers pushing for deterministic scoring + sensible defaults.
raj: +1. I sketched a minimal payload and behavior earlier, posting here for discussion.
marie: TL;DR we need: (1) clear top_k default, (2) normalized vs raw scores opt-in, (3) truncation policy that doesn't silently drop candidates.
simon: Also call out metrics and acceptance criteria — MRR/NDCG targets, latency SLOs.
emma: Agreed. Raj, can you paste the sample request?
raj: Sure — minimal example we prototyped:```
POST /v1/rerank
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "query": "How do I reset my password?",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "Click settings > password"},
    {"id": "c2", "text": "Use the forgot password flow"},
    {"id": "c3", "text": "Contact support"}
  ],
  "top_k": 5,             // client requested top results (optional)
  "score_mode": "normalized", // enum: "raw" | "normalized" | "logit"
  "normalize_to": {"min":0, "max":1}, // optional
  "truncate_behavior": "pad_or_truncate", // enum: "reject", "truncate", "pad_or_truncate"
  "candidate_context_limit": 1024 // tokens per candidate (server-side truncation)
}```
marie: A few thoughts on defaults: default top_k should be 3, not 5. Most customers only need top 1-3 and it helps keep token billing bounded.
simon: For scoring, IMO normalized by default is easier for clients. But we must be explicit about how normalization is done (softmax over logits? min-max over scores?).
raj: Implementation note: our model outputs a raw similarity/logit per (query, candidate). Options: (A) return raw logits only; (B) softmax across provided candidates (gives probability mass over set); (C) min-max normalize across candidates; (D) return both raw and normalized.
emma: Customer asks for both raw and normalized in the GA contract. That seems reasonable. Output payload could include `raw_score` and `score` (0-1).
olivia: Concern: if we do softmax normalization, scores change with candidate set size and composition. That can be surprising if clients pass different candidate pools between calls. We should document clearly.
marie: We also need a mode where scores are computed independently per candidate (e.g., sigmoid or model's calibrated prob) so they're stable across subsets. Maybe `score_mode: "independent" | "softmax" | "minmax"`
raj: Good call. We'll support `independent`, `softmax`, `minmax`. Default: `independent` for stability, but also return `softmax_score` if requested.
simon: Truncation policy: server-side truncation should never change candidate identifiers. If a candidate is truncated, include a `truncated: true` flag on that candidate and a `truncated_bytes` or `truncated_tokens` hint. If the query or candidate exceeds a hard limit and the request is in `truncate_behavior: reject` mode, return 400 with a clear error code.
emma: Launch guard: default to `truncate_behavior: reject` for GA for safety? That might cause failed requests for large customers. Maybe default to `pad_or_truncate` with a warning header on the response when truncation occurred. For strict customers, allow `reject`.
olivia: Ops note: any default that truncates silently will break fairness/regression tests. A warning header plus per-candidate `truncated` field is a good middle ground.
raj: Agreed. We'll emit `X-Rerank-Truncation: 1` header if any truncation happened and include `truncated_tokens` per candidate.
marie: Metrics and acceptance: define A/B metrics: NDCG@3 (target > baseline + 5%), MRR@1 improvement for search use cases, median latency p50 < 70ms for small candidate sets (<=5), p95 < 250ms. Also E2E correctness tests for score stability and ordering.
simon: Add canary rollout guard: if scoring normalization changes ordering vs previous release for >2% of sampled requests, auto-roll back. We have the pipeline to run live sampling.
emma: Good. Let's capture final launch decision items and owners.
raj: Action items: 1) API schema PR (adds `raw_score`, `score`, `score_mode`, `truncate_behavior`) — owner: raj — due EOD Thu (1764950000). 2) Docs: normalization semantics + examples — owner: marie — due Mon. 3) SDK changes (python/js) to expose both scores and truncation metadata — owner: olivia — due next Wed. 4) Telemetry + canary config for ordering regressions — owner: simon — due before canary.
marie: Acceptance criteria checklist: - default top_k=3 implemented and enforced server-side - both `raw_score` and `score` present when requested - `truncate_behavior` modes implemented and tested - response includes `truncated` flags + header when applicable - GA docs with examples and migration notes - performance targets met in benchmark job
emma: One more open question: do we allow streaming for rerank? Some teams want early partial results for long candidate sets. Thoughts?
raj: Streaming complicates normalization (softmax needs full set). Could support streaming in `independent` mode where each candidate is scored independently and returned as available. For GA we should mark streaming as alpha.
olivia: Ops: streaming alpha is fine — disable by default and require flag.
simon: I'll add metric instrumentation: NDCG, MRR, leaderboard of changed-order requests, and a daily digest to product.
emma: OK final call: default top_k=3; default score_mode=`independent`; return `raw_score` + `score` (0-1) when `score_mode != raw`; support `softmax` and `minmax` as options; `truncate_behavior` default `pad_or_truncate` with header; expose per-candidate `truncated` metadata; streaming alpha only. Raj to send PR today. Marie to draft docs.
raj: PR incoming — will post link once ready.
ops-bot: Deploy canary pipeline test scheduled for 1764880000; will alert on regression thresholds.
emma: Thanks everyone — will sync tomorrow if there are PR comments.
